Describe the steps needed to eliminate the variable [MATH: y] from this system by filling in the missing information below.

[MATH: \qquad] To eliminate [MATH: y,] multiply the [MATH: \,\textbf{__________}\,]equation by [MATH: \,\textbf{______}\,],
and add the equations.

sections.normalized_html:
Notice that the coefficient of [MATH: y] in the first equation is [MATH: 4,] while in the second equation it is [MATH: -2.]

If we multiply the second equation by [MATH: {\color{blue}2},] then the coefficient of [MATH: y] will turn into [MATH: -4,] which will cancel with the coefficient of [MATH: 4] in the first equation.

[MATH: {(3x + 4y = 2; (x − 2y = 4)× (2)]

Now, when we add the two equations, the variable [MATH: y] will be eliminated:

[MATH: 3x + 4y|= 2; 2x − 4y|= 8; (3x + 2x)|= (2 + 8); 5x|= 10] Therefore, the correct answer is the following:

To eliminate [MATH: y,] multiply the [MATH: \bbox[3pt,Gainsboro]{\color{blue}\text{second}}] equation by [MATH: \bbox[3pt,Gainsboro]{\color{blue}2},] and add the equations.
